disclaimer: General information only, not legal or financial advice. Claiming is always free on the official site.

entries.name: FCA Car Finance Commission Compensation Scheme
entries.case: FCA motor finance redress scheme (partly suspended pending legal challenge)
entries.eligibility: You used finance (including HP and PCP, not PCH leasing) for a car, motorbike or van between 6 April 2007 and 1 November 2024 and weren't told about a discretionary commission arrangement, a high commission or contractual ties. Exclusions apply.
entries.proof_notes: Complain to your lender for free. The FCA lists lenders and template letters. You don't need a claims company.
entries.estimated_payout: FCA estimate: average around £830 per agreement.
entries.administrator: Your lender, overseen by the FCA
entries.case_note: Payments are paused. The scheme's legal challenge is due to be heard 16–26 February 2027, and the FCA expects payments in 2027 if the scheme is upheld. Claims firms can take up to 36% (incl. VAT).

entries.name: Post Office Capture Redress Scheme
entries.defendant: Post Office / Department for Business and Trade
entries.eligibility: Sub-postmasters (or their estates or partnerships) who suffered a financial shortfall or other harm because of the Capture accounting software.
entries.proof_notes: Application form with a countersignatory. GOV.UK lists the required information.
entries.case_note: Open since 29 October 2025. No application deadline is stated on the GOV.UK page.

entries.name: Windrush Compensation Scheme
entries.eligibility: You suffered losses because you could not show your right to live in the UK, and you (or your parents or grandparents) came from a Commonwealth country before 1973, or you came from any country before 31 December 1988 and are now settled. Some close family members and estates can also apply.
entries.proof_notes: Evidence of losses (employment, housing, health, etc.).
entries.case_note: No closing date is shown on GOV.UK. Applying is free and information isn't used for immigration enforcement.

entries.name: Car Delivery Charges (RoRo shipping cartel) £55.8m Settlement
entries.defendant: MOL, NYK and other car shipping companies
entries.case: Mark McLaren Class Representative Limited v MOL (Europe Africa) Ltd & Others, 1339/7/7/20 (Competition Appeal Tribunal)
entries.eligibility: You (or your business) bought or financed a new car or van in the UK for your own use between 18 October 2006 and 6 September 2015 (some brands excluded). You can then claim for eligible new vehicles bought or leased up to 31 December 2019.
entries.estimated_payout: £25 for the first eligible vehicle, £5 each for the 2nd to 6th, £2.50 each after that. First come, first served until the fund runs out.
entries.case_note: Distribution Plan approved by the CAT (order 5 October 2026). The claim/distribution window has not opened yet; the official site says it will open in November 2026 and run about 6 months (or until the fund is used up). Sign up on the official site for an email when it opens. Separately, UK-domiciled class members may opt out (and non-UK members may opt in) by 6 November 2026 per the CAT order. Excluded brands include Audi, Fiat, Jaguar, Land Rover, Mini, Porsche, Seat, Skoda and Volvo, among others (see FAQs).

verification.method: WebFetch of official site + FAQs 2026-10-18; CAT Distribution Plan Order 5 Oct 2026 (opt-out/in by 6 Nov 2026; distribution Start Date not yet open)

entries.name: Google Play Store UK Developers £260m Settlement
entries.case: Professor Barry Rodger v Google (Competition Appeal Tribunal collective proceedings)
entries.eligibility: UK app developers who paid Google Play commissions during the claim period (see the settlement notice).
entries.case_note: Settlement approved at a hearing on 16 September 2026 (£260m). The official site still says details of how to claim will be published in the coming weeks; register there for updates. For developers, not ordinary app users.

entries.name: Kent v Apple App Store Overcharge Judgment
entries.defendant: Apple Inc. and Apple Distribution International Ltd
entries.case: Dr Rachael Kent v Apple Inc. & Apple Distribution International Ltd, 1403/7/7/21 (Competition Appeal Tribunal)
entries.eligibility: UK users of the App Store in the class (opt-out). Class members do not need to sign up to stay in the case.
entries.case_note: Judgment was delivered on 23 October 2025 ([2025] CAT 67), and the Tribunal refused Apple permission to appeal on 13 November 2025. A further amendment hearing was held on 27 May 2026 (judgment reserved) per the CAT case page. No distribution/claims process has started. Class members don't need to do anything now. Award amount and any Court of Appeal timetable were not confirmed on an official page.

entries.name: Merricks v Mastercard £200m Consumer Settlement
entries.case: Walter Merricks CBE v Mastercard (Competition Appeal Tribunal collective proceedings)
entries.eligibility: UK consumers in the class. The official site says you can register for a payment whether or not you ever held a Mastercard. Check the site for the exact class definition when claims open.
entries.proof_notes: The site says claims will use a simple online form.
entries.estimated_payout: Official site says individuals could get between £45 and £70 each.
entries.case_note: Settlement approved (CSAO made 31 October 2025). The Divisional Court dismissed the funder's judicial review on 10 June 2026. As of 18 October 2026 the official site still says the claims process has not started (pending a costs assessment). Leave an email on the site to be notified when claims open; official how-to-claim info will be posted there.

verification.method: WebFetch of official site 2026-10-18 (claims process not started; pending costs assessment)

entries.name: British Steel Pension Scheme (BSPS) Redress Scheme
entries.defendant: Financial advisers who advised BSPS transfers
entries.eligibility: You were advised to transfer out of the British Steel Pension Scheme between 26 May 2016 and 29 March 2018.
entries.proof_notes: Your adviser must contact you and review the advice. If the firm has failed, claim through the FSCS.
entries.case_note: Most reviews and offers were scheduled for 2023–2024. If you were never contacted, call the FCA helpline or complain to the Financial Ombudsman.
